---
title: "CRUD"
---

Add a complete feature to Init: database table → API router → UI. The todo feature is the reference implementation - this guide builds a `post` feature the same way. Copy the pattern, rename the nouns.

The full path touches four packages:

```
packages/db/src/drizzle-schema.ts             # 1. Table
packages/contract/src/post/post-schema.ts     # 2. Zod inputs
packages/contract/src/post/post-contract.ts   # 3. Procedure contract
packages/contract/src/index.ts                #    Register
packages/service/src/post/post-router.ts          # 4. Implementation
packages/service/src/root-router.ts               #    Mount
apps/web/src/app/.../posts/page.tsx           # 5. Server page
apps/web/src/app/.../posts/_components/       # 6. Client UI
```

## 1. Define the Table

```typescript
// packages/db/src/drizzle-schema.ts
export const post = pgTable.withRLS(
  "post",
  (t) => ({
    id: t.uuid().notNull().primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    organizationId: t
      .text()
      .notNull()
      .references(() => organization.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    title: t.text().notNull(),
    content: t.text(),
    createdAt: t.timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
    updatedAt: t.timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  }),
  (table) => [index("post_organization_id_idx").on(table.organizationId)],
);

// packages/db/src/drizzle-relations.ts
export const relations = defineRelations({ ...schemaAuth, ...schema }, (r) => ({
  // ...
  post: {
    organization: r.one.organization({ from: r.post.organizationId, to: r.organization.id }),
  },
}));
```

Every rule here matters: `organizationId` scopes the data to a tenant, the index makes the list query fast, `cascade` cleans up when an org is deleted, `pgTable.withRLS` keeps PostgREST locked out. See [Data Modelling](/docs/build/database) for why.

## 2. Push the Schema

```bash
pnpm db:push
```

No migration files, no codegen. Types flow from the schema definition immediately.

## 3. Validate Inputs

```typescript
// packages/contract/src/post/post-schema.ts
import { z } from "zod";

import { organizationInput } from "../organization/organization-schema";

export const createPostInput = organizationInput.extend({
  title: z.string().trim().min(1, "Title is required").max(255),
  content: z.string().optional(),
});

export const deletePostInput = organizationInput.extend({
  id: z.uuid(),
});
```

Org-scoped schemas extend `organizationInput`, so the `slug` is part of each procedure's declared contract - `requireOrganization` (step 5) reads the slug off the validated input.

## 4. Declare the Contract

The contract is what clients type against: input, output, error codes, and OpenAPI metadata. No handlers, no server imports.

```typescript
// packages/contract/src/post/post-contract.ts
import { post } from "@repo/db/drizzle-schema";
import { openapi } from "@orpc/openapi";
import { createSelectSchema } from "drizzle-orm/zod";
import { z } from "zod";

import { organizationBase } from "../base";
import { organizationInput } from "../organization/organization-schema";
import { createPostInput, deletePostInput } from "./post-schema";

const postRow = createSelectSchema(post);
const postOutput = z.object({ post: postRow });

export const postContract = {
  list: organizationBase
    .meta(openapi({ summary: "List posts", description: "...", tags: ["Post"] }))
    .input(organizationInput)
    .output(z.object({ posts: z.array(postRow) })),
  create: organizationBase
    .meta(openapi({ summary: "Create a post", description: "...", tags: ["Post"] }))
    .input(createPostInput)
    .output(postOutput),
  delete: organizationBase
    .meta(openapi({ summary: "Delete a post", description: "...", tags: ["Post"] }))
    .input(deletePostInput)
    .output(postOutput),
};
```

Register it in `packages/contract/src/index.ts`:

```typescript
export const contract = {
  organization: organizationContract,
  post: postContract, // Add here
  todo: todoContract,
  waitlist: waitlistContract,
};
```

`organizationBase` declares `NOT_FOUND` and `UNAUTHORIZED` and marks the operation as session-authenticated in `/openapi.json`. `list` needs nothing but the slug, so it takes `organizationInput` itself. If a client form needs the Zod schema at runtime, add `"./post/post-schema"` to `exports` in `packages/contract/package.json` (see `waitlist-schema`).

## 5. Implement the Router

```typescript
// packages/service/src/post/post-router.ts
import { post } from "@repo/db/drizzle-schema";
import { ORPCError } from "@orpc/server";
import { and, eq } from "drizzle-orm";

import { os, requireOrganization, requireSession } from "../orpc";

const authed = os.post.use(requireSession);

export const postRouter = {
  list: authed.list.use(requireOrganization).handler(async ({ context }) => {
    const posts = await context.db.query.post.findMany({
      where: { organizationId: context.organization.id },
      orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
    });

    return { posts };
  }),
  create: authed.create.use(requireOrganization).handler(async ({ context, input }) => {
    const [createdPost] = await context.db
      .insert(post)
      .values({
        organizationId: context.organization.id,
        title: input.title,
        content: input.content,
      })
      .returning();

    if (!createdPost) {
      throw new ORPCError("INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", { message: "Post was not created" });
    }

    return { post: createdPost };
  }),
  delete: authed.delete.use(requireOrganization).handler(async ({ context, input }) => {
    const [deletedPost] = await context.db
      .delete(post)
      .where(and(eq(post.id, input.id), eq(post.organizationId, context.organization.id)))
      .returning();

    if (!deletedPost) {
      throw new ORPCError("NOT_FOUND", { message: "Post not found" });
    }

    return { post: deletedPost };
  }),
};
```

`requireSession` goes on the implementer, so it runs before input validation and anonymous callers get `UNAUTHORIZED`. `requireOrganization` (in `packages/service/src/orpc.ts`) then resolves the org named by the validated `input.slug` and proves membership before any handler runs - so handlers just read `context.organization.id`. The router is a plain object: `os.post.router({...})` would re-apply `requireSession`, running it twice. Every mutation still filters by `organizationId` in the `where` clause, so a valid member of org A can never touch org B's rows.

Mount it in the root router:

```typescript
// packages/service/src/root-router.ts
export const appRouter = os.router({
  organization: organizationRouter,
  post: postRouter, // Add here
  todo: todoRouter,
  waitlist: waitlistRouter,
});
```

`os.router` fails to compile until every contract procedure is implemented with matching types. `orpc.post.*` now autocompletes in every app.

## 6. Build the Page

Server component: check the session, prefetch the query, hydrate.

```tsx
// apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/[slug]/posts/page.tsx
import { redirect } from "next/navigation";

import { PageHeader } from "@/components/header";
import { getSession } from "@/lib/auth-server";
import { HydrateClient, orpc, prefetch } from "@/orpc/server";
import { PostList } from "./_components/post-list";

const Page = async (props: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) => {
  const { slug } = await props.params;

  const session = await getSession();
  if (!session) {
    return redirect(`/auth/login?nextPath=/dashboard/${slug}/posts`);
  }

  prefetch(orpc.post.list.queryOptions({ input: { slug } }));

  return (
    <HydrateClient>
      <main className="flex flex-1 flex-col px-5 pb-5">
        <PageHeader>Posts</PageHeader>
        <PostList slug={slug} />
      </main>
    </HydrateClient>
  );
};

export default Page;
```

## 7. Build the Client Component

```tsx
// apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/[slug]/posts/_components/post-list.tsx
"use client";

import { toast } from "@repo/ui/components/sonner";
import { useMutation, useQueryClient, useSuspenseQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";

import { orpc } from "@/orpc/react";

export const PostList = ({ slug }: { slug: string }) => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  // Resolves instantly from the server prefetch - no loading spinner
  const { data } = useSuspenseQuery(orpc.post.list.queryOptions({ input: { slug } }));

  // Refetch this org's list after a write - each mutation invalidates only
  // what it touched; there's no global invalidate-everything net behind it
  const invalidatePosts = () =>
    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: orpc.post.list.key({ input: { slug } }) });

  const createPost = useMutation(
    orpc.post.create.mutationOptions({
      onError: (error) => toast.error(error.message),
      onSuccess: invalidatePosts,
    }),
  );

  return (
    <ul>
      {data.posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
};
```

The full reference - inline editing, delete confirmation, per-row pending states - is `apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/[slug]/(home)/_components/todo-list.tsx`.

## 8. Test It

Run the real router and middleware with a stubbed Postgres connection:

```typescript
// packages/service/src/post/post-router.test.ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { createRouterClient } from "@orpc/server";

import { createMockContext } from "../test-utils";
import { postRouter } from "./post-router";

test("rejects unauthenticated callers before querying", async () => {
  const context = createMockContext(null);
  const caller = createRouterClient(postRouter, { context });
  await assert.rejects(caller.list({ slug: "acme" }), { code: "UNAUTHORIZED" });
  assert.equal(context.query.mock.callCount(), 0);
});
```

```bash
pnpm -F @repo/service test
```

`todo-router.test.ts` checks tenant-scoped SQL, updates and missing rows. `auth/orpc-middleware.test.ts` covers missing organizations and non-members. Keep a live UI check for database constraints and persistence.

## Ship It Everywhere

Nothing else to do. The mobile app (`apps/mobile/src/utils/api.ts`) types its client with the same `ContractClient`, so `orpc.post.list` works there too. The extension and desktop shells open the web app itself, so they get the feature for free.

## Checklist

- Table has `organizationId` + index + `pgTable.withRLS`
- `pnpm db:push` ran
- Zod schema extends `organizationInput` and validates the feature's own fields
- Contract built on `organizationBase` with `.input()` and `.output()`, registered in `packages/contract/src/index.ts`
- Router built from `os.post.use(requireSession)`; each procedure `.use(requireOrganization)` and filters mutations by `organizationId`
- Router mounted in `root-router.ts`
- Page prefetches; client uses `useSuspenseQuery`
- Tests cover the unauthorized paths
